findings: Provider object request validation rejects malformed provider refs, bucket kind drift, invalid object refs, invalid KMS bindings, and actor drift before emitting receipts.
Targeted unit tests cover OCI put/get command shapes, provider receipts, provider-bucket drift, adapter config validation, and domain validation.
OCI-specific endpoint, namespace, bucket, and object-path behavior lives only in the adapter crate; domain owns the inward-facing port contract.
New StorageProviderObjectPort is additive; existing bucket/object/block domain constructors and tests remain unchanged.
No external SDK dependency added; deterministic adapter command structs follow existing workspace lint/test patterns.
Provider receipts carry provider_request_id and provider_evidence_ref for audit-chain correlation without raw object bytes.
Adapter command bodies carry object_body_ref/result_body_ref plus KMS/ciphertext refs, not raw object payload bytes or provider credentials.
Request translation is deterministic string assembly with no network call or allocation-heavy abstraction beyond canonical command construction.
Common provider object contract avoids duplicating provider-neutral validation inside each storage adapter.
ChangeSet is isolated to Cloud Storage domain additions, one adapter crate, catalog row, plan status, and evidence.
IP and phase index record OCI object request-contract green status and explicitly preserve block plus second-provider work as pending.
Avoids a false production claim: live OCI Object Storage smoke and full IP completion are not claimed.
Oya VCS claim accepted before writes; promotion remains through verify/done/promote.
FD-001 evidence, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain row identify the same ChangeSet id.
Kept provider-specific object storage behavior in a small adapter crate and a single provider-neutral port instead of branching OCI path logic into domain/API code.
No OCI SDK or runtime network dependency was introduced in this request-contract slice.
OCI Object Storage namespace/bucket/object command contracts are represented behind the same domain port expected for later providers.
Receipts carry provider request and evidence refs needed for later audit-chain correlation while live provider smoke remains explicitly pending.
